gaps.sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
gaps.explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me of leaking the story to the press.
gaps.explanation: Accuse somebody of + -ing. Blame uses 'for', thank and congratulate use different prepositions.

gaps.sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

gaps.sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
gaps.explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.
